dedupe_keys.name: critical infrastructure systems lab cornell reservoir storage and river basin datasets for southeast asia

description: The Critical Infrastructure Systems Lab at Cornell publishes a set of water datasets on its river basins page, mostly on reservoirs and rivers of Southeast Asia. The main one is a time series of water surface, storage and level for 185 large dams, each above 100 million cubic metres, in Mainland Southeast Asia from 1985 to 2023, described in an Earth System Science Data paper (MSEA-Res). The page also lists the input and output data to run the VIC rainfall-runoff model and its VIC-Res reservoir extension for the whole Mekong basin, 1981 to 2022, and for the Upper Mekong, 2005 to 2020; reservoir storage of the 10 largest Upper Mekong dams for 2008 to 2020; monthly streamflow reconstructions for the Chao Phraya basin, 1750 to 2003; a streamflow reconstruction of 62 stations in 16 countries over 813 years; and simulated hydropower for 1,593 dams. Coverage: regional, dam and basin scale. Access: free downloads through links on the page; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: the storage series are satellite-derived estimates, and file details were not opened. It supports reservoir operation, drought and hydropower simulations, and relates to the DAHITI satellite water level and Mekong River Commission portal records in the catalogue.
